diagnostic_evidence.quote: each row $i$ of $\matM$ is either real, or there exists another row $j \neq i$ of $\matM$ such that $\matM_{j,:} = \overline{\matM_{i,:}}$

issues.failure_explanation: The scalar inverse being purely imaginary does not determine when the product with the complex scalar x and the two complex entries is real; x can change the phase, and x=0 already makes the tube real regardless of m1 and m2. Thus the displayed if-and-only-if inference is false as written. The intended nonexistence conclusion instead follows from conjugacy of the two rows: for a real input tube, the two transform-domain coordinates are conjugates, so a vector (x,0)^T must have x=0.

failure_location.quote: therefore the tube $\matMi [x, 0]^\T$ is real if and only if $\overline{m_2}, \overline{m_1} $ have zero real part as well

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the real-part argument with the conjugate-coordinate argument: for real v, the second coordinate of Mv is the conjugate of the first, so Mv=(x,0)^T forces x=0.
issues.overall_effect: The justification for the example's feasibility conclusion is invalid, although that conclusion itself can be recovered.
issues.title: Invalid realness inference in the rank-truncation example
issues.why_classification: A short local replacement argument preserves the example's conclusion and no later formal result depends on the erroneous inference.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Showing that for all $j \in [r]$ there exists $k \in [r']$ such that $\bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \vec{\matW}_k^\CT \mm  \tU_{:,j} \neq \bs{0}$, hence $r' \geq r$.

issues.failure_explanation: Existence of some k for each j does not imply that the k's are distinct, so it does not imply r'>=r. The stronger cardinality claim is false: in a tubal ring with two real primitive idempotents e1,e2, take a diagonal tensor with singular tubes e1,e2 and identity singular-vector tensors. Its displayed generating set has two elements, but the single vector e1 E1+e2 E2 generates the whole image because the two idempotent coordinates of a ring element can be chosen independently.

failure_location.quote: The set $\{ \bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \tU_{:,j} \}_{j=1}^r$ is a minimal generating set for $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$ when considered as $\FFF_n$-module.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement to a generating set, or to an irredundant generating set if that is all that is needed, and remove the r'>=r cardinality conclusion; alternatively add hypotheses that force module rank r.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted minimum-size property of the tSVDM generating set is not established and is false in the stated generality.
issues.title: Minimal-generating-set cardinality claim is false
issues.why_classification: The result can be replaced by a nearby weaker module statement without affecting later formal results, but the claimed minimality guarantee is genuinely lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Being that the rank of a module is only defined for free modules, we cannot generally use it to measure the size of $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines module rank only for free modules and defines the relevant rank here over the principal ideal <e_j>, not over R_n. A nonzero module supported only on e_j is annihilated by 1-e_j and is generally not a free R_n-module, so rank_{R_n}(e_j X) is undefined as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace rank_{R_n}(e_j X) by the already defined rank over the principal ideal, or equivalently by the j-th tubal-length component of X.
issues.overall_effect: The stated identification between frontal-slice rank and the j-th tubal-length component is formally ill-defined, making the later multirank-length correspondence and its optimality applications unsupported until the notation is corrected.
issues.title: Undefined tubal-ring module rank is used in the rank-identification theorem
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and forced by the adjacent definitions; every downstream mathematical claim survives once the undefined rank symbol is replaced.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the number of nonzero coordinates of $\hbs{e}_j$ in the transform domain is exactly $d_j$

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma quantifies over all distinct idempotent blocks, but the counterexample assumes two indices in each block. When d_j=1 or d_h=1, the corresponding index set is a singleton. Identifying s with s' makes the coefficient real rather than an arbitrary complex Wirtinger variable, so the subsequent complex differentiation argument does not cover the (1,1), (1,2), or (2,1) cases.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add separate real-variable minimization arguments for the singleton-block cases and derive the same vanishing cross-Gram conditions.
issues.overall_effect: Necessity of orthogonality between rows associated with distinct idempotents remains unproved whenever either block is one-dimensional; consequently the necessity half of the main characterization has a missing quantifier case.
issues.title: Cross-idempotent necessity proof omits one-dimensional idempotent blocks
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial additional case analysis is needed; the expected main theorem can then be preserved without changing its scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then for any $j \in [\ell]$ and $k,k' \in \varsigma(j)$ it holds that $\thX_{:,:,k'} = \overline{\thX_{:,:,k}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For D=R+iI and the paper's inner product, <D,bar D>=||R||^2-||I||^2+2i<R,I>. Hence the preceding positive cross term expands with +2 Re(g)(||R||^2-||I||^2)-4 Im(g)<R,I>, not with the two displayed opposite signs. The second counterexample is also not a real tubal tensor: its s-face is conjugate(alpha)E2, whose conjugate is alpha E2, whereas its s'-face is -alpha E2, violating the paper's own conjugate-face lemma. The subsequent equality replacing 4 Im(g)Re(alpha)Im(alpha) by +2 Im(g) is also inconsistent with alpha=(1-i)/sqrt(2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the quadratic form with the correct signs and replace both counterexamples by conjugate-face-valid real tensors, then derive vanishing of both the real and imaginary parts of g_{s',s}.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not establish that rows associated with the same two-dimensional idempotent must be orthogonal, leaving the necessity direction of the main characterization unsupported.
issues.title: Intra-idempotent necessity counterexamples are algebraically invalid
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to this necessity lemma, but repairing it requires corrected calculations and replacement counterexamples rather than a typographical edit.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding identity contains D immediately after M0. The displayed substitution moves D to the other side of M1^{-1}, which is not valid for a nonuniform diagonal D because D and M1^{-1} generally do not commute.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the factors in their original order and use mode-3 associativity: (B x_3 M0 x_3 D) x_3 M1^{-1}=B x_3(M1^{-1} D M0)=B, since M1=D M0.
issues.overall_effect: The equality of multirank truncations, and consequently the fixed-rank error-equality theorem, lacks a valid derivation as written.
issues.title: Noncommuting transform factors are swapped in the normalized-truncation proof
issues.why_classification: A one-line factor-order correction restores the existing argument and preserves both the lemma and its dependent fixed-rank theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof identifies transform-domain retained energy under the nonunitary scaled transform M1 with original-domain Frobenius energy. These are not equal when D is nonscalar. The universal inequality is false: let n=3, let Q be the normalized DFT with one real row and one conjugate row pair, and let D=diag(3,1,1), which satisfies the block-scaling condition. Choose a real tube whose Q-domain squared magnitudes are (2,1,1). At gamma=0.9, M0 requires three components, while M1 has scaled energies (18,1,1) and requires only one. Thus r_gamma(M0)=3>1=r_gamma(M1), contradicting the theorem.

failure_location.quote: Then for all $\tX \in \RR^{m \xx p \xx n}$ and $\gamma \in (0,1)$, we have $r_{\gamma} (\matM_0) \leq r_{\gamma} (\matM_1)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must withdraw the universal ordering for nonuniform D and replace it with a substantially restricted or different statement that accounts for transform-domain energy reweighting.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed no-go guarantee that nonuniform row scaling always worsens energy-based compression is false, as are the prose conclusions that rely on that guarantee.
issues.title: Energy-rank comparison for scaled transforms is false
issues.why_classification: The theorem's central nonuniform-scale guarantee is false and no comparable universal claim is supported; restricting to uniformly scaled transforms would eliminate the advertised regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The input contract allows X=0. Then every singular value is zero and ||S_hat||_F^2=0, so the normalization on this line is 0/0 and r_gamma is undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit zero-input branch returning the zero approximation, or exclude the zero tensor from the input contract.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm does not deliver its stated output for an admitted boundary input.
issues.title: tSVDMII divides by zero on the zero tensor
issues.why_classification: A standard degenerate-case guard completely restores the algorithm's guarantee without changing its method or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The threshold nu_{r_gamma} may be attained only in other frontal slices. For a slice whose largest squared singular value is below the threshold, the displayed set is empty and its maximum is undefined. For example, with two slices of squared energies 100 and 1 and gamma=1/2, the threshold is 100 and the second slice receives no rho_i.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Initialize rho_i=0 and take the maximum over {0,...,min(m,p)}, or explicitly assign rho_i=0 when no singular value meets the threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm can fail to construct the advertised multirank vector and output tensor even for nonzero inputs.
issues.title: tSVDMII can leave a frontal-slice rank undefined
issues.why_classification: A local initialization convention fixes the boundary case while preserving the algorithm and its intended truncation guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: equipped with a scalar multiplication operation $\cdot : R \xx M \to M$ that is distributive over addition in both $R$ and $M$, and associative with multiplication in $R$

issues.failure_explanation: The listed module axioms do not imply 1_R m=m. For any nonzero abelian group M, the zero action r m=0 for every r satisfies the stated distributivity and associativity axioms but has 1_R m=0, not m. Only 0_R m=0 follows from the stated axioms.

failure_location.quote: It therefore holds that $1_R \cdot m = m$ and $0_R \cdot m = 0_M$ for all $m \in M$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard axiom 1_R m=m for every m in M to the module definition.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's definition of an R-module is materially weaker than the module notion used by the paper unless a unital action is intended.
issues.title: Module definition omits the unital-action axiom
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard local axiom restores the intended definition with no change to any construction, result, or guarantee.
